title: The VST captures three spectacular nebulae in one image
caption: The Eagle, Omega and Sharpless 2-54 nebulae, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: Eagle Nebula, M 16, M 17, Messier 16, Messier 17, Omega Nebula, Swan Nebula · constellation Serpens Cauda

recognition.text: Ranked #76 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Three glowing clouds of gas share this image from ESO's VLT Survey Telescope. On the right is the faint nebula Sharpless 2-54. In the centre sits the famous Eagle Nebula, Messier 16, and to the left is the Omega Nebula, Messier 17.
The image is enormous, containing three gigapixels, and takes in a wide stretch of sky at once.

The two Messier objects are well known, while Sharpless 2-54 is much less familiar. Together, the three make up only part of a vast complex of gas and dust. Inside it, new stars are forming, and their light makes the surrounding gas glow. Nebulae like these are stellar nurseries. Dense clouds collapse under gravity to form stars, and the hottest young stars then light up and sculpt the gas that remains into glowing shapes like these.

understand.summary: This image comes from the OmegaCAM camera on ESO's VLT Survey Telescope, using visible-light filters including one that isolates glowing hydrogen. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.

understand.eye: These nebulae are faint to the eye, and the camera's long exposures and hydrogen filter bring out glowing gas that would otherwise be hard to see.

explore: The VLT Survey Telescope is designed to photograph large areas of sky in detail, which makes it well suited to showing how separate, well-known nebulae belong to a single connected region of star formation.
alt: A wide view of three glowing nebulae of gas and dust side by side across a starry field.
